introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-001
items.detail: Design a centralized firewall management system for a university that manages firewall policies across academic, administrative, research, hostel, and guest networks.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: The system should allow authorized network administrators to create, review, update, and revoke firewall rules, enforce access restrictions between network segments, monitor blocked and allowed traffic, and generate alerts for suspicious or unauthorized communication attempts.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003
items.detail: The platform should maintain audit logs of firewall policy changes and administrative actions, provide a dashboard for reviewing network security events, and support multiple campus buildings.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: The solution should be secure, scalable, reliable, and manageable.

functional.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: design a centralized firewall management system for a university that manages firewall policies across academic, administrative, research, hostel, and guest networks.
requirements.statement: The system shall design a centralized firewall management system for a university that manages firewall policies across academic, administrative, research, hostel, and guest networks.

acceptance_criteria.given: A network administrator initiates policy management for the university's academic network
acceptance_criteria.when: The system receives a request to manage firewall policies
acceptance_criteria.then: The system returns a policy management interface accessible across academic, administrative, research, hostel, and guest networks
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the policy management interface response

unresolved_decisions: Which specific network segments are included in the policy scope?

requirements.title: allow authorized network administrators to create, review, update, and revoke firewall rules, enforce access restrictions between network segments, monitor blocked and allowed traffic, and generate alerts for suspicious or unauthorized communication attempts.
requirements.statement: The system shall allow authorized network administrators to create, review, update, and revoke firewall rules, enforce access restrictions between network segments, monitor blocked and allowed traffic, and generate alerts for suspicious or unauthorized communication attempts.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorized administrator accesses the firewall management interface
acceptance_criteria.when: The administrator creates a new firewall rule to restrict access from hostel to research networks
acceptance_criteria.then: The system enforces the access restriction.
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of traffic enforcement and rule application

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator observes traffic flow between academic and guest segments
acceptance_criteria.when: The system detects a blocked communication attempt from guest to academic network
acceptance_criteria.then: The system generates an alert for suspicious activity without terminating the connection
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of generated alert event

unresolved_decisions: Which actions trigger alerts? What constitutes 'suspicious' communication?
Is traffic monitoring continuous or periodic?

requirements.title: The platform shall maintain audit logs of firewall policy changes and administrative actions, provide a dashboard for reviewing network security events, and support multiple campus buildings.
requirements.statement: The platform shall maintain audit logs of firewall policy changes and administrative actions, provide a dashboard for reviewing network security events, and support multiple campus buildings.

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator modifies a firewall rule in the research network
acceptance_criteria.when: The system records the change as part of policy administration
acceptance_criteria.then: The audit log contains a timestamped entry with user identity, action type, and affected segment
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Inspection of audit log entries post-policy modification

acceptance_criteria.given: A security officer accesses the dashboard interface after policy updates
acceptance_criteria.when: The system renders a network security events overview
acceptance_criteria.then: The system renders a network security events overview
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of resulting dashboard display

unresolved_decisions: Which campus buildings are included in the dashboard coverage?
What data fields are displayed on the dashboard?

glossary.summary: Source-present terminology; definitions introduce no additional product obligation.

items.title: Policy
items.detail: A rule or decision governing permitted actions; its project-specific meaning remains defined by the source requirements.

items.title: Audit record
items.detail: A stored record of an event. Required event scope and retention are determined by the linked source, not this definition.

items.title: Log
items.detail: A collection of event records. This term does not itself require additional logging fields, events or access permissions.

items.title: Firewall
items.detail: A control that permits or restricts network traffic according to rules; mentioning it does not authorize automatic changes.

sdlc.justification: No differentiating input evidence is provided to select among Agile, DevSecOps, Spiral, V-Model, Waterfall, Hybrid, or Incremental models. All candidates receive equal suitability scores (40/100) due to absence of factors such as budget, delivery, failure consequences, feedback, legacy, regulation, schedule, stability, uncertainty, verification. The selection is therefore provisional and subject to later evidence.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
